//: Copy-paste detection config. Run it with `pnpm dupes`, which pins jscpd@5 — that pin, not anything in this file, is what fixes issue #911. Measured on the tree #911 read: jscpd@4 finds 3 clones, jscpd@5 finds 21, because v4 does not split a .svelte file into its script and template halves and so cannot see inside a Svelte component at all. The caps below are a separate hazard: each, left at its default, silently shrinks the answer with no warning and no exit code.
//minLines: 20 lines / 120 tokens is the 'meaningful clone' threshold: below it the report fills with import blocks and Svelte boilerplate.
//maxLines: Files longer than this are skipped SILENTLY — no warning, no exit code. jscpd v4 defaulted to 1000; v5's default is higher but undocumented, so pin it rather than inherit it. Measured on this repo: at 1000 the report is 4 clones, lifted it is 8. Half the answer, no indication anything was dropped.
//maxSize: Same silent skip, by bytes rather than lines (default 100kb). Currently inert here — jscpd splits a .svelte file into its script/template/style halves before this check, so no unit exceeds it even though RecipeViewPage.svelte is 165kb on disk. Pinned as a guard against the next big file, not as a fix for a live miss.
//format: Scopes which FILES are picked up. It does not stop jscpd splitting a .svelte file into its :typescript / :html / :css halves — those are compared regardless, which is what makes template duplication visible at all.
//ignore: Tests are excluded deliberately. Arrange/assert repetition across test files is desirable, and including them buries the real findings under hundreds of test-to-test clones.
